title: Polynomial-time local-unitary equivalence of graph states
abstract: Local-unitary (LU) equivalence asks whether two quantum states differ only by independent changes of basis on their qubits. For graph states, whether this relation can be decided in polynomial time has remained open for over a decade. We give a deterministic algorithm that decides LU equivalence for graphs on $n$ labelled vertices in $\widetilde O(n^{6.38})$ bit operations and constructs exact single-qubit unitaries whenever the states are equivalent. Building on Claudet and Perdrix's quasipolynomial algorithm, we replace the enumeration of vertex subsets by a compact system of constraints generated from pairs and triples. The remaining graph transformation is found by solving linear equations over the binary field. These new steps cost $\widetilde O(n^5)$ bit operations; the inherited graph preprocessing sets the overall bound. We also count the local-Clifford (LC) classes of graph states within any LU class: their number is a power of two, computable within the same bound. For any given graph state, this decides whether single-qubit Clifford gates reach every graph state in its LU class, and supplies a counterexample when they do not. The method also decides LU equivalence of stabilizer codes encoding one logical qubit.
summary: This paper presents a deterministic, polynomial-time algorithm to solve the local-unitary equivalence problem for graph states. By reformulating the problem using linear constraints over the binary field, the authors achieve a complexity of $\widetilde O(n^{6.38})$. This advances the understanding of quantum state classification and has implications for stabilizer codes and quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the long-standing open problem of determining whether two graph states are Local-Unitary (LU) equivalent, meaning they differ only by independent changes of basis on their qubits.
main_result: A deterministic, polynomial-time algorithm is presented that decides LU equivalence for graph states in $\widetilde O(n^{6.38})$ bit operations and constructs the necessary single-qubit unitaries if equivalence holds.
method: The method builds upon prior quasipolynomial algorithms by replacing vertex subset enumeration with a compact system of linear constraints derived from pairs and triples, solved over the binary field.
model_or_system: The study focuses on graph states, which are quantum states defined on $n$ labeled qubits by applying controlled-Z gates corresponding to the edges of a graph $G$. The equivalence is tested for the state $|	ext{H}angle = e^{i\phi/n}  igotimes_{v=1}^n U_v |Gangle$.
key_observables: LU equivalence, the number of local-Clifford (LC) classes within an LU class, and the explicit single-qubit unitaries $U_v$ realizing the transformation.
important_parameters: The size of the graph, $n$, which dictates the polynomial complexity bound $\widetilde O(n^{6.38})$.
main_assumptions: The algorithm assumes the graph state is prepared via the standard CZ gate procedure, and the complexity analysis relies on solving linear equations over the binary field.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the LU equivalence problem, contrasts it with simpler Clifford equivalence (LC), and then details the algorithmic steps: using a standard form, applying incidence closure, and solving the remaining graph transformation via affine linear systems.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, efficient algorithmic solution to a fundamental classification problem in quantum information theory, which is crucial for understanding the limitations and structure of quantum error-correcting codes.
